evals.prompt: What is the real test result of the latest build on branch dev/datev-feed-receipts? Give me the tally line and any ERROR lines, and say which build id you read.
evals.expected_output: Names a specific build id and branch read live from the odoo.sh dashboard, with the branch confirmed from the page's own heading rather than assumed from a constructed URL; quotes the odoo.tests.result tally line verbatim plus the module's own odoo.tests.stats line; lists any ERROR-level lines found in install.log, or states plainly that none were found; treats the status badge only as a secondary signal, never as the verdict; reads the whole log rather than only the tail; performs no push, rebuild, or deploy.

evals.prompt: A build card on odoo.sh says 'At least one test failed when loading the modules (de_fin_mail)' but the log says 0 failed, 0 errors. Explain what is going on and what to check.
evals.expected_output: Explains that odoo.sh fails a module on any ERROR-level log line during its tests, independent of the pass/fail tally, citing the confirmed build 38535645 case and the assertLogs fix pattern; instructs grepping install.log for ERROR-level lines (not just the tally) and checking whether each one is deliberate (a guard method under test) versus a real failure; does not conclude the build is simply broken, and does not propose rebuilding or redeploying anything.

evals.prompt: I need RPC access to the dev build of branch X to look at a record. What do I do, step by step, without touching production?
evals.expected_output: Gives the ordered steps: find the build and open its Connect link, set a throwaway password via the documented JSON-RPC fetch call against /web/dataset/call_kw while the Connect session is active, then connect over XML-RPC (xmlrpc.client) using that build's own URL and database name read live from the dashboard; notes that setting the password invalidates the browser session; states clearly that every step targets only the dev build's own database, never a dataegret-odoo-prod-* database, and includes no write, deploy, or rebuild against production.
